analyst_view.overall: Early view: two sides near the 24th-place line for the knockout play-offs: Egnatia (26th, two points) and Lincoln Red Imps (22nd, three points). Egnatia drew with Midtjylland and at AGF before losing 2-0 at Craiova, and Lincoln beat Hajduk Split 1-0 in Gibraltar after defeats by Brann and Twente. Enea Bitri's sending-off came in that Craiova game, a UEFA match, so the ban should apply here. I found no domestic news for either side, so this rests on European form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: each of Egnatia's three European games ended with two goals, and Lincoln's win over Hajduk was 1-0. With both sides close to the cut-off line and a point not useless to either, I expect a cautious game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.9 for Egnatia. Egnatia at home should have more of the ball against a Lincoln side that sat deep against Hajduk, which the split already reflects; I read nothing to move the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean a little higher: this is a direct fight for a play-off place between two sides on two and three points, and Egnatia finished their last European game with a man sent off (Enea Bitri, per the brief and ESPN's event list). Tight, high-stakes games of this kind usually draw more fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots, 18.2 of them for Egnatia. I lean lower: Egnatia have scored two goals in three European games and do not look like a side that piles up attempts, and Lincoln defended deep and well against Hajduk. A cagey game should mean fewer shots than the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. For the same reasons as the goals and shots, with two modest attacks and a lot at stake, I lean slightly lower.
